message.content: how does the wrap layer keep a half-selected row's syntax colors?

content.text:
## Rows, runs, and the selection

A row is cut at the **union** of its style runs and the selection's ends, so a
*half-highlighted* wrapped row keeps every color it had. The cut lives in `row_line`, and
the offset each row starts at rides along in `Row::start`.

- Painted rows carry their character offset — that is what resolves the caret.
- A rendered table selects linewise; ~~a column there~~ names no source character.
- See [the wrap module](https://example.com/wrap) for the measure it wraps at.

> Nothing looks selected until you select something.

```rust
fn row_line(row: &Row, style: &LineStyle, selection: Option<Range<usize>>) -> Line<'static> {
    let cuts = style.boundaries().chain(selection.into_iter().flatten());
    cuts.fold(Vec::new(), |mut spans, at| {
        spans.push(Span::styled(row.slice(at), style.at(at)));
        spans
    })
    .into()
}
```

| construct | selects | sent as |
| --- | :---: | --- |
| prose | by character | stripped text |
| table | by line | original pipes |
| card | nothing | — |
